files_modified: textbrush/references/normalize.py (round 2: renamed to textbrush/references/normalization.py -- F13; module content also changed, see implementation_notes)

implementation_notes.module_layout: textbrush/references/normalization.py (renamed from normalize.py in round 2, see rename_and_module_layout below) holds all logic; __init__.py re-exports the public surface (normalize, NormalizedReference, the six-member exception taxonomy, SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS, NEUTRAL_FILL_VALUE). Zero internal textbrush.* imports in normalization.py -- confirmed by an AST-based import-graph test reusing tests/test_config.py's _internal_imports() helper (that helper's own docstring names this as the intended template for S3), not by manual review.
implementation_notes.signature_decision: normalize() takes (path, target_size: tuple[int, int] | None = None), not the single-argument normalize(path) stories.json's seam description literally writes. Remediation round 1 (Decider ruling 2026-09-18, findings F1/F2): target_size is now OPTIONAL, not required as the prior round shipped it. spec.md sec 6.2 items 3 and 4 (uniform resizing; padding to a fixed rectangular canvas) are each conditional on the selected model ('when required by the selected model', 'when a fixed rectangular tensor is required'); a required parameter silently promoted both to unconditional, which this leaf module has no standing to decide. target_size=None applies EXIF orientation, RGB conversion, and alpha compositing only, returning the image at its EXIF-corrected source dimensions -- the safe default, since a forgotten argument now yields an unpadded image S5's model-boundary assertion catches loudly, rather than a canvas silently padded to a guessed size. The prior round's claim that S7 resolves target_size 'via S2's per-model registry data' was factually false (ModelSpec at textbrush/model/registry.py has no dimension field) and has been corrected: the fact 'model X's pipeline accepts reference inputs at dimensions D' is owned by inference (S5), exposed as a reference_input_size(...) accessor on the InferenceEngine instance per stories.json blocking condition S5-BC-1, NOT by a slug-keyed table and NOT by S2's ModelSpec. references still does not import model or inference and holds no per-model dimension table of its own, preserving its leaf status; S7 is the pass-through conduit. The NormalizedReference field list itself (the part every downstream story depends on byte-for-byte) is unchanged.
implementation_notes.pixel_data_representation: NormalizedReference.pixel_data is a PIL.Image.Image (RGB mode, exactly target_size), not a numpy array or tensor. Chosen because it matches this codebase's existing convention (textbrush/buffer.py and textbrush/inference/base.py already use PIL.Image.Image for image data) and is what diffusers reference-editing pipelines accept directly, avoiding a new array-library dependency for this story.
implementation_notes.neutral_fill_reuse: NEUTRAL_FILL_VALUE (128, mid-gray) is used for BOTH alpha compositing and centered padding. Remediation round 1 (finding F6): the prior round's claim that 'the spec does not require these to be the same value' was backwards and has been corrected in the module docstring, architecture.json, and here -- spec.md sec 6.2 BINDS alpha-fill and padding-fill to one value ('composited onto the same documented neutral fill'). The code (one constant for both) was already correct; only the three justifications describing it as an optional simplification were wrong and have been replaced with a citation to that binding (ledger concept neutral-fill-binding), so a later story reading them cannot conclude it is safe to split the constants.
implementation_notes.scaling_algorithm: _scale_and_pad computes exactly one scalar `scale = min(target_w/source_w, target_h/source_h)` applied identically to both axes (a letterbox/pillarbox 'contain' fit, never crops), then centers the result via floor-division margins -- a single extra pixel of odd remainder deterministically lands on the right/bottom. Verified via a bounding-box measurement in tests (not a re-derivation of the same formula in isolation): a per-axis-independent-stretch bug would fill the ENTIRE canvas with content whenever source/target aspect ratios differ, which the bounding-box tests would catch as a mismatch against the expected padded-content dimensions. Remediation round 1 (finding F5): the prior round's `max(1, round(source_axis * scale))` clamp silently stretched degenerate axes (verified repro: a 4000x3 source into a 512x512 canvas rendered content at 512x1 -- an actual 512:1 ratio -- while content_aspect_ratio kept reporting the true 1333.33, a field lying about the pixels it accompanies). That clamp is removed; `_scale_and_pad` now raises NormalizationError, naming the source and requested dimensions, whenever either scaled axis would round below 1 pixel. Round 1 also reinstated a second, narrower clamp (`scaled_width/height = min(scaled, target)`) to guard against float-rounding overshoot at the fitted edge; round 2 (N6) removed that clamp entirely rather than keep a justification for it, after a 2,000,000-trial randomized search over (source_w, source_h) in [1,8000]^2 and (target_w, target_h) in [1,4096]^2 found zero cases of `round(source_axis * scale) > target_axis` on the bottleneck axis -- the clamp was unreachable dead code, consistent with this project's 'do not handle impossible scenarios' rule (already applied to F14 in this same round).
implementation_notes.failure_taxonomy: Six exception classes under a common ReferenceImageError base (named to avoid shadowing the Python builtin ReferenceError): UnsupportedExtensionError, ReferenceNotFoundError, UnreadableReferenceError, CorruptReferenceError, ReferenceResourceConstrainedError (Pillow's real DecompressionBombError, its DecompressionBombWarning tier, or MemoryError during decode), and NormalizationError (the degenerate-scale case, a MemoryError surfacing during the scale/pad stage specifically, or -- per round 2's N4 docstring fix -- the degenerate-aspect-ratio rejection itself, which is not a resource condition and is now named as its own cause rather than left implied only by 'within available resources'; all three are distinct from decode-time failures per spec.md sec 11's separate 'normalization failure' error). Remediation round 1 (finding F4): the prior round only translated the error tier of Pillow's decompression-bomb guard; between 1x and 2x MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS Pillow instead emits a bare DecompressionBombWarning and proceeds to decode, which under warnings-as-errors would escape the ReferenceImageError hierarchy entirely (uncaught by S7's acknowledgement-time handler, AC-STATE-3/AC-RECOVERY-1). Round 1 closed this gap via `warnings.catch_warnings()` + `simplefilter('error', Image.DecompressionBombWarning)`; round 2 (N3) replaced that with a deterministic header-only size check against `Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` (see decompression_bomb_check_rework) because the warnings-filter approach mutated global, non-thread-safe interpreter state on a codepath that runs concurrently with worker/delivery threads. Both tiers still reach ReferenceResourceConstrainedError.
implementation_notes.mutability_contract: Remediation round 1 (finding F3): `@dataclass(frozen=True)` never protected the mutable PIL.Image.Image that `pixel_data` points to -- an external `.paste()`/`.putpixel()` would silently corrupt every later read of the same held instance (relevant to S7's decode-once-per-acknowledged-configuration lifetime, spec.md sec 6.3). Fixed by stating the no-mutate-without-copy rule as an explicit CONTRACT line in the class docstring rather than deep-copying on construction/access (which would cost memory per generation for a hazard fully addressed by documentation), and by declaring `eq=False` so comparison is by identity, explicitly. Round 2 correction (N1): the ORIGINAL justification for `eq=False` given here and in the class docstring was itself factually wrong on two of its three points, and has been corrected in both places. `PIL.Image.Image` DOES define value equality (`Image.__eq__` compares mode/size/pixel bytes -- two independent normalizations of the same file DO compare `==` True), so the original 'PIL images have no value equality' claim was false; the real cost is that auto-generated `__eq__` would run an O(pixels) comparison on every `==`, and `decoded_at` (excluded from the determinism invariant) would make whole-dataclass equality meaningless regardless -- two instances from identical bytes a second apart would compare unequal on `decoded_at` alone. The `hash()` TypeError is real, but its cause was misstated: it is `unhashable type: 'Image'` because PIL defines `__eq__` without `__hash__` (the standard Python rule), not an 'unhashable dict in Image.info'. The `eq=False` DECISION is unchanged by this correction -- only its reasons were wrong. tests/test_references.py's determinism tests already compared via `pixel_data.tobytes()`, unaffected by eq=False.
implementation_notes.decompression_bomb_fixture_strategy: Rather than committing a multi-hundred-megapixel fixture to the repository to trigger Pillow's real decompression-bomb guard, tests monkeypatch the real PIL.Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS threshold down below an existing small fixture's actual pixel count, so the REAL Pillow safety mechanism fires against real decode -- not a simulated failure -- while keeping the fixture set small. Documented as a deliberate choice in the test docstring in case a future reviewer expects a literal huge fixture file.
implementation_notes.unreadable_fixture_strategy: The permission-denied fixture is NOT committed to the repository (git does not reliably preserve permission bits across checkout, and a CI/dev environment running as root would bypass them entirely, making a static fixture non-portable). Instead, tests/test_references.py builds it at test time via tmp_path + shutil.copy + chmod(0o000), and skips (does not silently pass) on non-POSIX platforms or when running as root.
implementation_notes.boy_scout_note_recorded_not_fixed: Pillow (PIL) is formally listed only under pyproject.toml's optional [model] extra, but textbrush/buffer.py and textbrush/inference/base.py already do unconditional `from PIL import Image` at module scope -- meaning Pillow is already a de facto hard dependency of the core package regardless of that formal listing, predating this story. This story adds a third unconditional PIL import (references/normalization.py) but does not change pyproject.toml, since correcting that pre-existing declaration/usage mismatch is a config-ownership decision outside a leaf-module story's scope -- flagged here for the lead rather than fixed unilaterally.
implementation_notes.remediation_round_2: Second and final remediation round: 4 new findings (N1-N4, N6) introduced or missed by round 1, 2 hygiene items (N5, F12), a concurrency fix (N3), a dead-code removal (F14), 2 missing tests (F10, F11), and a rename (F13) carried over from round 1's un-dispatched batch. Disposition: N1 (module renamed normalize.py -> normalization.py, see rename_and_module_layout below); N2 fixed (eq=False's justification in NormalizedReference's docstring was factually wrong on two of its three claims -- PIL images DO define value equality via Image.__eq__, and the TypeError comes from the absence of __hash__, not an unhashable Image.info dict -- replaced with the honest cost/decoded_at-meaninglessness rationale, the eq=False DECISION itself unchanged); N3 fixed as a real code change (see decompression_bomb_check_rework below); N4 fixed (NormalizationError's docstring now names the degenerate-aspect-ratio cause alongside the resource-exhaustion cause); N5 fixed (VQ-S3-011 in verification.json marked SUPERSEDED, pointing at VQ-S3-F2's accurate optional-target_size record); N6 resolved by removing the min(scaled, target) clamp entirely rather than keeping a fixed-up justification -- 2,000,000 randomized (source_w, source_h, target_w, target_h) trials across [1,8000]x[1,4096] found zero cases where round(source_axis * scale) exceeds target_axis on the bottleneck axis, so the clamp was dead code triggering the same 'do not handle impossible scenarios' principle already applied to F14; F9 dropped per lead's instruction (reviewer concurred, no action taken); F10/F11/F12/F13/F14 as described in their own notes below.
implementation_notes.rename_and_module_layout: F13 (naming, lead decision): textbrush/references/normalize.py renamed to textbrush/references/normalization.py. The prior name collided with its own primary export -- `textbrush.references.normalize` meant both the submodule and, after __init__.py's `from .normalize import normalize` re-export, the function object -- forcing tests/test_references.py to import the module via importlib.import_module('textbrush.references.normalize') / sys.modules rather than a plain `import textbrush.references.normalize as normalize_module` (which would have silently resolved to the function). Renaming the module removes the collision outright: the test file now does a plain `import textbrush.references.normalization as normalize_module`, and the surprised_by note from round 1's retrospective is resolved, not merely worked around. Updated: textbrush/references/__init__.py's import statement and module-docstring cross-reference; tests/test_references.py's import, the two forbidden-import assertion messages, and the internal-imports assertion in TestModuleBoundary; scripts/generate_reference_fixtures.py's module-docstring cross-reference; architecture.json's private_files entry. The public import surface (`from textbrush.references import normalize, NormalizedReference, ...`) is unchanged -- confirmed by tests/test_references.py's own import block and TestModuleBoundary passing unmodified in intent. NOT touched: stories.json's `files` list for S3 still names normalize.py (lead-owned per this round's constraints, not edited) and ownership-ledger.json (also lead-owned); verification.json's historical remediation-round-1 answer text still cites normalize.py by its name at the time each answer was written and was deliberately left as-is (it documents what was true when written, not the current file layout) except for VQ-S3-011, which N5 required to be marked superseded regardless.
implementation_notes.decompression_bomb_check_rework: N3 (concurrency_hazard, code change): _decode() no longer wraps Image.open()/.load() in warnings.catch_warnings() + simplefilter('error', ...) to promote Pillow's 1x-2x DecompressionBombWarning tier into an exception. That pattern mutates CPython's global warnings-filter list (documented as not thread-safe) and restores the entire filter list, not just the one entry it added, on __exit__ -- a real hazard given `references` decodes on the IPC command thread while worker and delivery threads run concurrently in this codebase's threading model. Replaced with a deterministic, state-free check: Pillow's own `_decompression_bomb_check()` (verified by reading Pillow's source, PIL/Image.py) runs the 2x-error-tier check *inside* `Image.open()` itself, against the header-reported size, before any pixel data is read -- so that tier still raises DecompressionBombError from `Image.open()` exactly as before, caught by the same except clause. For the 1x-2x warning tier, `_decode` now reads `image.size` (available immediately after `Image.open()`, from the header) and raises ReferenceResourceConstrainedError directly when `Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS is not None and width * height > Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` -- the identical threshold Pillow's own check uses, computed independently rather than relying on Pillow's warning machinery. Verified: the existing 1.6x-ratio warning-tier test (test_decompression_bomb_warning_tier_also_raises_resource_constrained_error, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS=100_000 against a 400x400=160,000-pixel fixture) still passes and still discriminates -- 160,000 > 100,000 trips the new direct check. The `warnings` import is no longer used and was removed.
implementation_notes.test_additions_round_2: F10 (missing_test): added TestTargetSizeValidation with a parameterized test over three malformed target_size values -- (0, 64) zero width, (64, -1) negative height, (64,) wrong arity (its ValueError comes from tuple-unpacking itself, not the explicit positivity check, and is asserted the same way since the docstring only promises ValueError, not a specific origin) -- plus a dedicated test confirming target_size=None reaches neither the unpacking nor the positivity branch. F11 (missing_test): added test_composited_alpha_fill_and_padding_fill_coexist_on_one_canvas to TestAlphaCompositing, normalizing the 200x100 valid_alpha.png fixture onto a 300x300 canvas (scale 1.5, scaled content 300x150, 75px top/bottom padding bands) and asserting BOTH a padding-band pixel and a composited-alpha-region pixel (deep in the source's formerly-transparent right half, well clear of the content seam and canvas edge) equal _FILL_RGB, with a sanity check that the opaque left half survives scaling unchanged -- the only test that would catch a later story splitting NEUTRAL_FILL_VALUE's two uses into different constants (ledger concept neutral-fill-binding). F12 (doc_drift): removed a stale two-line comment in test_odd_remainder_padding_tiebreak_is_deterministic_right_bottom describing a toy '3x1 source into a 4x1 target' example that no longer matches the test body (600x400 source into a (601, 400) target); the correct description already existed two lines below it and was left in place.
implementation_notes.dead_code_removed_round_2: F14 (dead_code): `if oriented is not None: image = oriented` after `ImageOps.exif_transpose(image, in_place=False)` (round 2's own reading of PIL/ImageOps.py:673-703 confirms `in_place=False`, the default and the only mode used here, always returns an Image.Image, never None -- None is returned only under `in_place=True`) was unreachable. Reduced to `image = ImageOps.exif_transpose(image)` per this project's 'do not handle impossible scenarios' rule, with a one-line comment recording why the guard was removed rather than just silently deleting it.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The seam description in stories.json and the architecture.md seams array both write the source artifact as the literal one-argument form `normalize(path) -> NormalizedReference`, but nothing in spec.md, acceptance-criteria.md, architecture.md, or stories.json specifies where the model's required reference-input dimensions come from -- spec.md sec 5.5's six presets are explicitly OUTPUT dimensions, never reference-input dimensions, and NormalizedReference's own field list has no model or target-size field. Implementing padding to 'the model's required dimensions' (spec.md sec 6.2 item 4) is impossible without that information arriving from somewhere. This is a genuine, load-bearing gap in the epic's artifacts as written, not a matter of implementer taste -- but it is also squarely a signature-shape decision within this story's stated authority as the seam's creator, so I resolved it (target_size as a required second parameter) rather than escalating with AWAITING_SPECIFICATION, and documented the reasoning in three places (architecture.json's signature_decision, the normalize() docstring, and verification.json's VQ-S3-011) so S5/S7 -- and the lead -- can override the decision cheaply if they disagree, without needing to rediscover the gap themselves.
retrospective.surprised_by: textbrush/references/__init__.py's `from .normalize import normalize` line rebinds the `textbrush.references.normalize` package attribute from the submodule object to the function object, because both share the literal name 'normalize' -- a classic Python submodule/symbol name collision. This meant `import textbrush.references.normalize as normalize_module` in the test file silently resolved to the wrong object (the function, not the module), which the AST-boundary test then failed against with a confusing AttributeError until diagnosed. Worked around in tests via `importlib.import_module('textbrush.references.normalize')`, which goes through sys.modules directly rather than attribute traversal. Not a defect in the production module (the public API deliberately exports `normalize` as the primary consumer-facing name, which is exactly the intended usage for S5/S7), but worth flagging since it will bite anyone else writing introspection code -- rather than ordinary consumer code -- against this package.
